text:
Carla: heads up — after the python/ts SDK opt-in sampling change, the console quota dashboard is showing ~30% of internal-proxy traffic as "unattributed". noticed while triaging tenant X.
Ben: oh no, which sampling change? the compact header one? :grimacing:
Carla: yeah, the sampling seed moved from route_hint -> compact-meta. SDKs send the new key only when opt-in is enabled, but the console expects the legacy key for attribution fallback.
Alice: that matches what I saw in the QA run. dashboard mapping code only checks x-route-hint then falls back to tenant header. new compact header is x-route-meta-compact.
Dan: quick question — why wasn't the proxy shim mapping this? I thought internal-proxy normalizes route headers before ingest.
Erin: proxy currently strips unknown headers for safety. we didn't whitelist x-route-meta-compact because it was marked experimental in the SDK RFC.
Carla: problem is some customers enabled new SDK flag in prod. result: their traffic lands with compact header only, proxy drops it, console shows unattributed quota. customer unhappy.
Ben: short-term fix: add a mapping in the proxy that converts x-route-meta-compact -> x-route-hint when present. low-risk and reversible.
Dan: agreed. we can push a proxy config change and a small console mapping tweak. infra-bot: scheduled change requires rollout window and owner.
Carla: owner: Dan. target: canary to infra region A in next 30m, full rollout in 3h if stable. will need release notes.
Alice: longer-term, SDKs should send both headers for N releases (compat window) and then deprecate legacy. propose SDK flag behavior: when opt-in is true, send compact header and legacy header with sampled=false marker.
Ben: can we instead have the console accept compact header too? reduces proxy touchpoints.
Erin: console is slower to release; proxy is faster and central. but agree we should update console mapping in parallel.
Dan: plan: 1) proxy shim mapping in 30m 2) console mapping PR concurrently 3) SDK patch to dual-write headers in next minor release 4) migration docs + console notice
Carla: will draft customer-facing note: "If you enabled compact metadata in SDKs, we will map it for quota attribution automatically. Please update to SDK >= next-minor for best results."
Ben: sample quickfix command for proxy feature flag toggle:
```
# enable compact->legacy mapping in proxy
curl -X POST https://infra-api/flags/proxy.map_compact_to_legacy -d '{"enabled":true}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN"
```
Alice: question: does mapping risk misattribution if someone intentionally uses compact to indicate different routing semantics?
Dan: good point. compact contains a routing fingerprint plus sampling bits. mapping will preserve the fingerprint but set a compatibility tag. we'll add a header like x-route-hint-sourced: sdk-compact so console can treat mapped entries differently for analytics.
Erin: I'll add that tag in the proxy change. console PR should ignore the tag for quota attribution but surface it in telemetry logs for audits.
Carla: test plan: run canary for 2h, verify unattributed rate drops to baseline and no error spikes. also check billing ledger reconciles.
release-bot: Deploy v0.32.1 to python-sdk succeeded for canary group beta-testers :rocket:
Ben: after SDK dual-write and proxy mapping we can plan a deprecation schedule: 60 days notice, then remove legacy emission in next major.
Carla: agree. I'll file the migration doc and support playbook. tagging @support for customer comms.
Erin: pinging console team leads for PR review. I'll open the proxy config change now.
Carla: thanks everyone — keeping this in thread for audit. :thumbsup:
